label: copy-phase re-input of k/o/u/p late in long sequences
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (100% of mass), when the fed-back input token is one of a small set, led by k (42% of mass, 11x lift), then o, u, p, and more weakly r, t, a. It is silent during the original phase and at the delimiter, never fires for recall_idx < 3, and fires mostly at absolute steps t >= 12, so long sequences (L = 8-9) dominate. The strongest activations are k or o re-inputs around recall_idx 3-4. Context tokens also matter: when the neighbouring tokens (prev_tok or out_tok) are in {v,m,h,x,z,3} precision goes above 0.8, but that cuts recall a lot. Most late k/o/u/p copy steps stay inactive (precision about 0.33), so the predicate gives the support of the unit but not its exact selectivity. It does not fire on digits or other letters in the copy phase.
